analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts equilibrium phase fractions and austenite (FCC_A1) thermodynamic stability versus temperature, indicating the gradient between hot-rolling (1150 °C) and tempering equilibria
analytical_models.model_note: Shows that for 12Al alloys the austenite (FCC_A1) stability is lower at 800 °C than at 1150 °C, used to explain tempering-induced austenite decomposition.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase amounts (mol) computed as a function of temperature (0–1300 °C) for the 12Al-30Mn-1C composition
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD thermodynamic equilibrium calculation of phase amounts vs temperature

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting and casting into ingots
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Resulting ingots had a mass of 0.5 kg.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: 5 kg load applied for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled (as-received) reference state obtained by hot-rolling the as-cast ingot at 1150 °C to 5 mm and water quenching; the study does not present dedicated micrographs of the hot-rolled 12Al-30Mn-1C condition (microstructural characterization focuses on the 600 °C and 800 °C tempered states).

unmapped_findings: Nominal composition of the alloy is 12 wt% Al, 30 wt% Mn, 1 wt% C, Fe balance, which falls within the tested ranges of Table 1 (Al 9–12, Mn 10–20–30, C 0.4–1 wt%).

This sample represents the hot-rolled (as-received) reference condition (hot-rolling at 1150 °C to 5 mm flat products followed by water quenching), which is the baseline to which all 600 °C and 800 °C tempering treatments (30 min, water quenched) are compared.
For the same alloy (12Al-30Mn-1C) the 800 °C tempered condition reached 352 HV (Table 5), but that value belongs to a different (tempered) sample and is not part of this hot-rolled sample.
Minitab18 software was used to verify the consistency of acquired hardness data, with outliers excluded before plotting.

The paper reports that at 800 °C the 12Al-30Mn-1C austenite grains were fully spinodally decomposed with the finest and least dense acicular κ-carbide network (Fig. 8(e),(f)), but these findings pertain to the tempered state, not to this hot-rolled sample.
